Subject: Launch traffic variance & quota operations — HealthScope ramp (Apr 12-14)

Team —

HealthScope has confirmed a production ramp that could exceed their current quota during the first 36 hours after go-live. I attached their traffic forecast and the latest MAP for context. Quick summary: they expect a peak of ~400 rps sustained for short bursts (3–5 minute windows) with an average session size of ~420 tokens. They're aiming for go-live on Apr 12 with a 72-hour monitoring window.

Ask: can we provision a temporary quota uplift (short-lived bump + rollback plan) and confirm routing/fallback policy? Specifically I need:
- Ops: concrete rate-path proposal (max multiplier, ramp cadence, circuit-breaker thresholds).
- Product: any constraints around model variants (prefer quantized), token caps per request, or SLOs that would block an uplift.
- Sales/CS: confirm committed PO/purchase contact and whether HealthScope will accept a graded canary or needs an all-in cold cut.

Attachments: healthscope_traffic_forecast_Q3_2027.csv, MAP_HealthScope_v2.pdf

Timeline: need a decision + runbook by EOD Apr 8 to lock capacity reservations.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin

Marcus — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the MAP. Quick notes from the sales side: HealthScope has verbally committed to the PO (procurement@healthscope.com is processing paperwork) but they will not accept any visible downtime during the transition — they prefer an orchestrated ramp with a short canary period.

From our last call with Alex: they plan a staged cutover (10% traffic -> 50% -> 100%) over roughly 2–3 hours once they see stable latency under 300ms. That said, their traffic forecast includes sudden 3–5m spikes during feature flag activations (we saw this pattern in staging).

Proposed mutual action plan (high level):
1) 48h prior: reserve dedicated burst slot and pre-warm models.
2) Canary: 10% for 30–60m, observe latency/err rates.
3) Ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 2–3 hours if stable.
4) Fallback: automatic route to 8bit-quant model family if latency > 500ms for 5m or error rate > 1%.

I'm looping Alex on this thread to keep procurement and their SRE in the loop. Alex, please confirm whether HealthScope will accept the staged ramp above and whether the PO will include a reserve for burst minutes.

—Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[MAP reference: MAP_HealthScope_v2.pdf (application/pdf)]

Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch traffic variance & quota operations — HealthScope ramp (Apr 12-14)

Thanks — useful context. A few product constraints and asks so ops can build a safe path:

1) Model variant: HealthScope is currently on the 13B-fin-mix variant. For launch we strongly prefer they stay on the quantized 13B-q8 variant to reduce memory pressure; we can allow a temporary switch to a float-16 variant only if SRE confirms GPU availability and the customer agrees to transiently higher cost.

2) Token accounting: if sessions average 420 tokens, ensure per-request token limits are enforced at 1k tokens to avoid explosion from clients that batch.

3) Prefix caching: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompt scaffolds — this will materially reduce per-token load. Ops, can you set TTL=6h for KV caches for this tenant?

4) Monitoring hooks: Product asks for automated sampling (1%) of responses for QA and a baseline prompt set run before canary and after ramp. Please provide a shared Drive link with the result artifact.

5) Rollback triggers: Product requests that any sustained P50 latency regression >20% vs baseline for 10m triggers an automatic rollback to previous version. Ops and sales should align on these numeric thresholds.

If you want, I can prepare a short runbook with the required flags and a minimal checklist.

-Neha
Product Manager, Serving Runtime
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
[link: https://docs.redwood.com/runbooks/launch-rate-paths]

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch traffic variance & quota operations — HealthScope ramp (Apr 12-14)

All — ops notes and a concrete rate-path proposal below. I'm calling out what we can safely commit to given current capacity and what needs explicit capacity reservation.

Operational guardrails (proposal):
- Pre-warm: provision dedicated slot (4x GPU units) from Apr 11 00:00 to Apr 15 00:00. This requires capacity sign-off (I can file the reservation ticket once we confirm the PO).
- Rate-path: allow 2.5x baseline for the first 4 hours after canary success, then ramp to 3.5x for the next 20 hours. Circuit-breaker at 4x sustained for >5 minutes will trigger immediate throttling and route to a smaller model family.
- Fallback: automated fallback route to 13B-q8-first (lowest-latency quantized variant) when P95 latency > 500ms for a rolling 5m window OR when error rate > 1% for 2m.
- Token caps: enforce per-request token cap at 1,000. Any request that exceeds will be rejected with 413 and metric tagged.
- KV caching: set TTL=6h for tenant, but note this will consume cache memory; we need confirmation on memory reservation.
- Support: require an on-call SRE during the first 48h after ramp with a dedicated phone bridge. I can provide the rotation but need Marissa to confirm CS coverage for customer communication.

Constraints:
- If HealthScope insists on float-16 model family during peak we need explicit GPU burst capacity and a cost uplift; this is currently not in the draft PO.

Next steps:
1) Marcus/Marissa: confirm PO timing so I can file the capacity reservation ticket.
2) Karthik/Marissa: confirm canary window and who will coordinate on-call with the customer.
3) Neha: I will implement the TTL and sampling hooks once the reservation is in place.

-David
Site Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.ai

Thanks everyone — summary and owners. Please treat this as the locked runbook we will present to HealthScope:

Summary decisions:
- Capacity: Marcus to confirm PO (HS-3492) by Apr 9 EOD. Once PO is confirmed, David will file a capacity reservation for the 4x GPU slot (Apr 11-15).
- Rate-path: approved as David proposed (2.5x -> 3.5x, circuit-breaker at 4x).
- Model: HealthScope will be on 13B-q8 for the ramp; float-16 only with explicit capacity/cost uplift.
- Token caps & KV caching: per-request cap 1,000; KV TTL=6h.
- Monitoring & rollback: sampling + QA prompt set before canary; rollback triggers: P95 >500ms for 5m or error rate >1%.
- Support: Marissa to own customer comms and SRE bridge coordination for the first 48h.

Owners & next steps:
- Marcus (owner): confirm PO, update HS procurement, share signed SOW. Deadline: 2027-04-09 17:00 PDT.
- David (owner): file capacity reservation ticket immediately after Marcus confirms PO; pre-warm the slot on Apr 11.
- Neha (owner): publish the runbook checklist and provide the QA prompt set artifact before canary.
- Karthik & Marissa: coordinate the canary schedule with HealthScope SRE and customer communications.

Alex / procurement@healthscope.com: please confirm the PO timing and whether the PO will include a line item for burst capacity. If you want, we can set up a 30m call tomorrow to finalize.

I'll send the finalized runbook (short PDF) to HealthScope once actions are complete.
